title: WallpaperDB · Renderer measurements
schema_note: Run records in summary.json omit the plots field. The standalone index.html embeds that field with 100 ms binned traces; all other statistics and provenance are shared.

method.cpu: Percent of one logical core: 100% is one fully occupied core. Aggregate CPU is the median of valid runs' supported time-weighted process CPU-counter means, not a mean of instantaneous samples. Native evidence or a retrospective audit matched by raw-report SHA-256 and run name must support each mean. Sampled peaks/tails need their own coverage evidence. Unsupported CPU metrics and plots stay null; presentation/resource measurements may remain valid. Each CPU metric reports its contributing run count.
method.groups: Group by study, batch, build and engine/case. Invalid and zero-measurement runs are retained but excluded from aggregates. Each aggregate median/range describes per-run values; a median of per-run p99 values is not a pooled/global p99.
method.presentations: Delivered FPS and interval distributions come from compositor presentation feedback. Missing WebKit feedback stays null; browser callback snapshots are retained separately and never substituted for delivered FPS.
method.missed_target_slots: Estimated missed target slots per minute are derived from sum((sequence increment - 1) * count) only for a conventional physical connector in monitor evidence, positive sequence increments, and a target within 1% of recorded refresh. This estimates unfilled refresh slots between observed presentations, not individually traced lost frames. Virtual/zero sequences and other target-to-refresh ratios remain null.
method.browser_callbacks: Initial telemetry is captured before warmup, final telemetry after measurement. Newer reports also retain a post-warmup measurement-initial snapshot, sampled before the timed interval starts. These snapshots do not provide exactly aligned counter endpoints for measurement-window FPS. Reported browser FPS values are snapshots only. Native mpv telemetry FPS is container metadata and is excluded from browser callbacks.
method.video_progress: Playback progress evidence is copied from the profiler, including its method, status and limits. Native media-update counts describe libmpv render-update submissions; browser playback-quality counters describe video display accounting. Neither is a compositor-presentation or independently measured decoder count. Presentations can reuse a retained media texture, so a high delivered FPS need not mean equally frequent media updates. Media render-update rate is shown only for a native media path with recorded update evidence; static images, scenes without media and uninstrumented browser/mpvpaper media paths remain unavailable.
method.content_behavior: A retained static image may remain visible with zero new presentations after warmup. Recorded zero is preserved; absent feedback stays null. A paused case records a pause request, whose verification and scope come from pause_evidence. Zero frames or browser callbacks alone do not prove pause, decoder inactivity or stationary pixels.
method.plots: Presentation plots retain the MAXIMUM interval in each 100 ms bin. CPU and activity/resource plots retain sampled maxima; free RAM/VRAM plots retain minima. Empty bins are absent, not zero. Plots cannot recover exact hitch timing or event order inside a bin; the original statistics and relative raw-report links remain available.
method.gpu: GPU activity, memory activity, power, temperatures and graphics clocks describe the whole sampled NVIDIA device/desktop, not a single process. NVML activity integrates its native coarse sampling window. OS CPU-frequency descriptors are not proof of throttling.
method.resources: Free VRAM and MemAvailable minima are derived from measured-window gpu_timeline samples before discarding that timeline. They do not describe unobserved between-sample minima or pre-measurement guard activity.
method.comparison: Read output, source, requested/effective FPS, renderer, recorder, pointer, background-activity and source/binary hash evidence together. A virtual display measures rendering/compositor feedback, not physical scanout. Lower CPU at a lower delivered rate does not establish higher efficiency.
method.portability: summary.json contains statistics and provenance without plot traces. index.html embeds the same records plus 100 ms binned plots and remains standalone. Neither artifact includes full-resolution timelines. Raw links are relative to this output directory; keep the original study folders in that relative position to use them. Machine-local paths and process IDs are removed from copied provenance.

manifest.scanout: Contender output DP-2; wallpaper output WDB-STRESS. Resolve physical/virtual output and adapter from monitor/renderer evidence; no 4K physical scanout is implied.
manifest.gpu_utilization_limit: NVML native utilization windows are approximately 1/6–1 second. Safety/resources poll at 4Hz even with sample-hz=0; GPU memory_percent is memory activity, vram_* fields are allocation.
manifest.cpu_counter: Linux process clocks, 20Hz; includes exited threads within sampled processes. Membership frozen after warmup; short-lived newly spawned children may escape accounting.
manifest.cpu_frequency_limit: scaling_cur_freq logical-policy min/mean/max sampled at 1Hz; descriptive OS frequency values, not per-process executed clocks or proof of thermal throttling.
manifest.background_cpu_limit: Two /proc snapshots per run estimate average CPU of surviving other processes, excluding measured families/compositor/profiler. Activity above 50% of one core is flagged, not automatically invalidated; short-lived background processes can be missed.
manifest.feedback_clock: CLOCK_MONOTONIC actual presentation timestamps. Per-output event counts define FPS. A sequence gap >=2 is not inherently late when target FPS is below physical refresh.

guard_policy.note: CPU boosting near 95C is normal for this 7950X; the default 96C sustained threshold is an anomaly guard.

source_evidence.algorithm: sha256(sorted(relative pathname length, pathname, file length, file bytes)); 8-byte big-endian lengths

manifest.gpu_utilization_limit: NVML native utilization windows are approximately 1/6–1 second. Safety/resources poll at 4Hz even with sample-hz=0; GPU memory_percent is memory activity, vram_* fields are allocation.
manifest.cpu_counter: Linux process clocks, 20Hz with per-PID elapsed intervals and raw clock evidence; includes exited threads within sampled processes. Membership frozen after warmup; short-lived newly spawned children may escape accounting.
manifest.cpu_frequency_limit: scaling_cur_freq logical-policy min/mean/max sampled at 1Hz; descriptive OS frequency values, not per-process executed clocks or proof of thermal throttling.
manifest.background_cpu_limit: Two /proc snapshots per run estimate average CPU of surviving other processes, excluding measured families/compositor/profiler. Activity above 50% of one core is flagged, not automatically invalidated; short-lived background processes can be missed.
manifest.feedback_clock: CLOCK_MONOTONIC actual presentation timestamps. Per-output event counts define FPS. A sequence gap >=2 is not inherently late when target FPS is below physical refresh.
manifest.pause_evidence_limit: Paused dynamic cases require periodic and boundary pause flags, stopped native counters/trace work, and fresh browser heartbeat reports with stable host scene events and observed video positions. Unknown evidence invalidates the pause comparison. A paused-only 1 Hz browser report timer contributes to measured paused cost; rAF/OSR callbacks, arbitrary JS/CSS animation, decoder activity and pixel stillness are not equated with these observations. Retained static images do not require continuing presentation.
manifest.video_evidence_limit: Playback positions and optional browser total-minus-dropped video frame counters establish observable playback, not compositor FPS or decoder counts. Native CSV media events count libmpv render-update submissions. Unsupported evidence stays unavailable; event-driven images are exempt.
